meta.title: Queueing theory for packet buffers: M/M/1 and Little's law
meta.tools: Event-driven simulation of a single-server queue (Poisson arrivals, exponential service), M/M/1 formulas, Little's law, finite buffers and loss probability (M/M/1/K), a deterministic-service comparison (M/D/1)
meta.summary: Simulate a router buffer, verify the M/M/1 predictions for queue length, waiting time and their blow-up as load approaches 1, confirm Little's law, size a finite buffer for a target loss rate, and show how deterministic packet lengths halve the waiting time.
meta.problem: A link is 90 % utilised. How long do packets wait, and how large must the buffer be to lose fewer than one in a million?
meta.theory:
M/M/1 with load ρ = λ/μ: mean number in system L = ρ/(1−ρ), mean time W = 1/(μ−λ); Little's law L = λW (for any stable queue). Finite buffer K (M/M/1/K): loss $P_K=\frac{(1-ρ)ρ^K}{1-ρ^{K+1}}$ ⇒ K ≈ ln(10⁻⁶)/ln ρ ≈ 131 at ρ = 0.9. M/D/1
(constant service): waiting time in queue $W_q=\frac{ρ}{2μ(1-ρ)}$, half the M/M/1 value — variability, not load alone, creates delay.
meta.method:
Lindley recursion for waiting times, 10⁶ packets per load, ρ = 0.1…0.95; time-average number in system from the sample path; finite-buffer simulation for K = 10…40 at ρ = 0.9 (losses counted directly where
measurable) and the formula extrapolated to 10⁻⁶.
